tasks.goal: A new package services/api/app/narrative with three pure parts. (1) collector: given a period ('bu hafta' = the last 7 days, 'bugün', 'dün', or explicit start/end in UTC) and an optional device word (ev / ofis / bulut / a device name), read the activity ledger through the existing read-only query in app/ledger/service.py (query / latest - read that file first; do not change it) and produce a NarrativeFacts dataclass: failed events FIRST (each with its subsystem, summary and the reason the ledger holds), then completed events grouped by subsystem, counts per subsystem and per device, no_capable_device events, and the period actually covered. Deterministic: the same rows give the same facts. (2) narrator: a Protocol `Narrator.tell(facts) -> str` with a RuleNarrator that writes Turkish sentences from the facts alone (no model call in this task; the model narrator is a later task behind the same Protocol) - about 30 seconds of speech, failures first, then what was done, then counts; an empty period says 'bu dönemde kayıt yok'. (3) auditor: `audit(facts, text) -> Verdict` that REJECTS a narrative in which any failed event is not mentioned (match by its summary words), any completed subsystem is missing, or a number appears that is not one of the facts' counts; and `repair(facts, text)` that appends the missing failure sentences deterministically. The public entry is `tell(db, period, device=None, narrator=None) -> str` = collect → narrate → audit → repair. Read docs/DECISIONS.md ADR-0201 and the ledger vocabulary for the event types and statuses; use their constants by import, never string copies. Work only inside the area. No new dependency. Python 3.12, ruff clean, tests under services/api/tests/unit run with `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest <file> -q` from services/api. Every test name is a sentence about behaviour; every rule has a near miss beside its hit; one mutation per rule shown RED and the file restored by sha256 (never git checkout --).

tasks.goal: A new package services/api/app/execution holding the execution_target decision as pure functions - nothing here talks to a device, a database or a model.
